The biggest trade on an LNG construction site is not welding. It is driving.

On Alaska LNG, the Alaska Department of Labor puts truck drivers at 3,519 of 11,850 direct hires — more than pipefitters, welders and insulators combined. Trucks move the bulk materials, the smaller modules, the equipment and the people, across an 807-mile pipeline, eight compressor stations and two plants. The plan estimates 250 to 270 trucks running at peak.

Read the number honestly: it is one American project with unionised labour. No Gulf or African LNG project publishes its workforce trade by trade — we checked the impact assessments for Mozambique, Papua New Guinea, Ichthys, Gorgon and Wheatstone, and they all publish a peak total and stop. So take the order as the shape of a big construction job, not as a headcount for Ruwais.

What you actually need: Defensive Driving appears in QatarEnergy's contractor HSE regulations as a required course, arranged by the contractor. Before that, a valid licence issued in the host country — TÜV SÜD will not even certify a forklift operator in Qatar without a current Qatari licence first.

What we could not find: any government source setting out heavy-vehicle licence categories or conversion rules for Saudi Arabia, the UAE or Qatar. If someone quotes you those rules with confidence, ask where they read them.

Full detail and sources in the link in bio.

posts.instagram:
The second biggest trade on the job, and the one most often filled locally.

Alaska LNG: construction labourers and helpers, 2,311 of 11,850 direct hires. This is the work every other trade depends on — moving material, preparing access, assisting riggers and fitters, keeping the work front clear. Papua New Guinea LNG's national content plan lists labourers first among its construction positions.

If you are applying from abroad, know what you are up against here. On Mozambique LNG, CCS JV states that employment priority goes to Mozambican nationals who meet project requirements, and its own subcontractor figures show what that means in practice: catering, 1,300 of 1,340 workers Mozambican; camp construction, 350 of 600. That is not a barrier put up against you, it is how national content policies are written, and it is public.

On certificates: for general labouring there is no requirement from any issuing body we could find. If someone offers to sell you a labourer's certificate, there is nothing behind it.

If you will assist lifting operations, OPITO has two real entry standards — Banksman & Slinger, and Rigger. Both 24 guided learning hours, valid two years and eight months. Read OPITO's own wording before you pay: the certificate "does not imply competence". It is stage one of three, followed by supervised logged experience and only then an assessment.

posts.instagram:
There is no pipefitter certificate. Not in any country, from any issuing body.

We went looking for one, because it is sold constantly. There is no personnel certification standard for pipefitting anywhere we could find. The tickets on a piping crew belong to the welder, not to the fitter. If a training centre or an agent offers you a "certified pipefitter" qualification, they are selling a document no employer recognises, because none exists.

What does exist is the code the work is built to. On an LNG or refinery site that is usually ASME B31.3, which governs materials, design, fabrication, assembly, erection, examination and testing of process piping in refineries and cryogenic plants. Knowing that code, and being able to read an isometric, is what actually gets you kept on.

The number: Alaska LNG counts pipefitters, welders and insulators together at 1,566 of 11,850 direct hires. The published figure does not separate them, so we are not going to.

When it mobilises: with the first big construction peak. On Alaska LNG that peak — around 4,200 workers — is described as heavy civil and welding-intensive pipeline trades.

Full detail and every source in the link in bio.

posts.instagram:
6G is a position, not a certificate.

It means the pipe is fixed at 45 degrees and you have to work all the way around it — the most demanding of the four test positions. You do not get "a 6G". You get a welder qualification, taken in the 6G position, under a code. Anyone selling you "a 6G certificate" on its own either does not know the subject or is counting on you not knowing it.

The three codes that matter, and what each one actually does:

ASME BPVC Section IX covers qualification of welding procedures, and per ASME's own course material for the section, performance qualification of welders and welding operators.

ISO 9606-1 qualifies the person, not the procedure. Its stated focus is your ability to manipulate the electrode or torch by hand and produce an acceptable weld. Manual and partly mechanised fusion welding of steels — fully automated welding is excluded.

AWS D1.1 is the structural steel code: procedure and welder qualification, fabrication, workmanship, inspection and acceptance for load-bearing steel.

Which one you need follows the work. Pressure and process piping sits under ASME. Structural steel sits under AWS.

The number: Alaska LNG counts welders with pipefitters and insulators, 1,566 of 11,850 direct hires.

posts.instagram:
There is no Gulf rigger licence. There is no Gulf crane licence either. Neither exists in any form.

This is the role where that phrase is used most often to sell something worthless, so here is how it actually works. The client sets the requirement, project by project. QatarEnergy requires lifting personnel — rigging supervisors, riggers, crane operators, forklift operators — to be certified against its own technical regulations, not against an international scheme. A different client on a different project will want something else.

What does exist is third-party certification bodies operating inside the Gulf. TÜV Rheinland's Qatar scheme LPC-005 certifies rigger, banksman, rigging supervisor and lifting supervisor: minimum age 18, 15 to 20 hours of training, written and practical exams at 70 percent, certificate valid between one and three years. The scheme itself states that any additional client requirements still have to be met on top of it.

One thing that gets misquoted constantly: LEEA's own qualifications are for lifting equipment engineers and inspectors, not for crane drivers. When QatarEnergy asks whether lifting personnel hold LEEA or equivalent, it is asking about inspectors.

The number: around 1,300 heavy equipment operators of 11,850 direct hires on Alaska LNG.

We never ask for money for jobs.

posts.instagram:
This trade mobilises last. Which is exactly why most people apply too early, hear nothing, and give up.

The clearest published evidence we found: on Alaska LNG the first construction peak, around 4,200 workers, is described as heavy civil and welding-intensive pipeline trades. The second peak, around 4,500 in 2029, is mechanical and electrical-intensive facility construction. Electrical and instrumentation follows civil and piping. If you are applying at the same time as the welders, you are applying two years early.

What governs the work: an LNG plant is an explosive atmosphere, and that single fact drives the qualifications. The two recognised ones are CompEx Ex01 to Ex04 — installation, inspection and maintenance of equipment where gas and vapours are present, UKAS accredited, core competence valid five years — and the IECEx Certificate of Personnel Competence, twelve units from basic awareness through installation, maintenance, inspection and design.

Now the honest part. Both are widely respected, but we could not find a single Gulf client document naming either as contractually mandatory. Useful and real, not provably compulsory. We would rather tell you that than let you assume.

The number: 397 electricians and instrument fitters of 11,850 direct hires on Alaska LNG.

We never ask for money for jobs.

posts.instagram:
Train at the wrong centre and the card cannot be issued. Not later, not after an upgrade, not ever.

CISRS states it plainly: it will only issue a card for training and assessment carried out at a CISRS accredited centre. Scaffolding training anywhere else does not convert and does not count. This is the single most expensive mistake in this trade, and it is entirely avoidable — check the centre against the CISRS list before you pay, not after.

The route built for workers outside the UK is CISRS OSTS, the Overseas Scaffolder Training Scheme, running on the same principles as the UK scheme. Accredited centres operate in Abu Dhabi, China, India, Ivory Coast, Kazakhstan, Nepal, Nigeria, Oman, Qatar and Trinidad. Levels 1 to 4, plus scaffold inspection and supervisor.

Worth understanding what the card is and is not. QatarEnergy's contractor regulations require scaffold to be erected, altered or dismantled only by a qualified scaffolding contractor to its own requirements — they do not name CISRS. The card is what gets you hired by the contractor. It is not itself the client's rule.

No published source gives a headcount for scaffolders on any project, and we are not going to invent one. Our own read, labelled as ours: scaffolders arrive with bulk mechanical and piping work and stay through commissioning, because insulation, painting and punchlisting all need access.

We never ask for money for jobs.

posts.instagram:
One NDT certificate travels with you between employers. The other one does not. Know which you are being sold.

ISO 9712 is third-party certification: an independent body examines you, and the certificate is yours. Valid five years, and it moves with you when you change company.

ASNT's SNT-TC-1A is different in kind. ASNT itself states that certificates based on it are employer-based programmes for which ASNT does not hold responsibility, and that you are certified by your employer, under your employer's written practice. Change employer and you generally start again. It is not a lesser document — it is a different thing entirely, and plenty of good inspectors hold one. But if you are paying for a certificate expecting it to be portable, ask which scheme it is under first.

What the levels mean, since this also gets misrepresented. Level 1 carries out tests under written instructions and under Level 2 or 3 supervision, and cannot select the method or assess results. Level 2 chooses techniques, calibrates, interprets and evaluates. Level 3 takes responsibility for the facility, the procedures and the staff.

On welding inspection: CSWIP 3.1 needs three years of verified welding inspection experience to sit, two theory papers and a practical on eight specimens, 70 percent on every part, valid five years. AWS CWI is three parts at 72 percent each plus a vision test, valid nine years with renewals at three and six.

We never ask for money for jobs.

posts.instagram:
OSHA says its own card is not a certification and is not required. Those are OSHA's words, on OSHA's website.

"The Outreach Training Program is voluntary and OSHA does not require Outreach training." And: "an OSHA card is not considered a certification or license." People are sold OSHA 10 and OSHA 30 every day as a requirement for Gulf work. They are not a requirement for Gulf work. They are a US awareness programme, and the body that runs it says so.

What a Gulf client actually demands, in its own words. QatarEnergy's corporate HSE standard requires HSE advisers to hold at least one of: a NEBOSH Certificate or Diploma; Chartered Membership of IOSH; a Diploma in Occupational Safety and Health Management or membership of IIRSM; or Registered Safety Professional status. On top of that, its own competence assessment.

Note what that list names on the IOSH side. It is chartered membership — CMIOSH — not the three-day Managing Safely course. Those are very different bars, and the course is often sold as though it were the qualification.

NEBOSH's International General Certificate is a qualification: two units, an open-book scenario examination with a closing interview, a practical risk assessment, a minimum of 63 taught hours.

No published source gives a headcount for HSE officers on any project. We are not inventing one.

We never ask for money for jobs.

#oilandgas #HSE #safety #EPC #energyjobs

No ticket exists for this job. We looked properly, and there is nothing to require.

No issuing body and no employer document we could find sets a certification requirement for a site materials controller. General supply-chain qualifications exist — CIPS, APICS CPIM — but we found no evidence that any EPC contractor asks for them for this role. What counts is experience with a materials management system and with preservation requirements, and that is learned on a site, not bought.

We are telling you this because the absence is the useful information. If someone is selling you a warehouse or materials certificate as the thing standing between you and a job in the Gulf, there is no standard behind it.

The job itself: receiving, preserving, storing and issuing everything the site installs, and knowing where all of it is. The Alaska Department of Labor treats material handling and logistics as two of the ten occupational groups significant to pipeline construction. Papua New Guinea LNG lists store managers among its construction positions.

No published source places warehousing in a construction phase. Our own read, labelled as ours: it has to start before bulk construction, because material must be received and preserved before it can be installed, and it carries on into commissioning for spares.

That is the last of the ten. All of them, with every source, at the link in bio.

We never ask for money for jobs.
